$comment: ELF64 POSITION-INDEPENDENT EXECUTABLE (PIE: ET_DYN + PT_INTERP + entry) for aarch64 Linux -- c171 conformance (the arm64 sibling of elf64-x86_64-linux-pie). CONFIG-ONLY: the PIE arm of `src/link/format/elf.cpp` is arch-agnostic -- `isPie = isDyn && processExit.has_value()` (entry-cluster PRESENCE, not a new elf.type value), DF_1_PIE + the interpreter are read from this schema, and the synthesized `_start` trampoline is the shared, fully target-driven `entry_trampoline.cpp` builder (it reads the CC via `callingConventionByName("aapcs64")` and every instruction via `opcodeByMnemonic` -- the arm64 EXEC already drives this exact trampoline). So this needs NO writer code, only this schema. Like the x86_64 PIE: `elf.type = dyn` routes to `encodeElfExecDynamic`; the entry cluster flips the `isPie` sub-mode (PT_PHDR + PT_INTERP + `.interp`, non-zero base-relative e_entry, DT_FLAGS_1 = DF_1_NOW | DF_1_PIE); the kernel execve's it at a randomized base (full-image ASLR under ld-linux-aarch64). Everything else stays the arm64 dyn shape: base-0 VAs the loader slides, R_AARCH64_RELATIVE for internal absolute data slots, symbol-based absolute relocs for extern-address data slots, got-indirect extern DATA imports, real-named .dynsym exports. THE DISCRIMINATOR from the .so sibling (elf64-aarch64-linux-dyn) is ENTRY-CLUSTER PRESENCE, not a new elf.type: a PIE IS ET_DYN. POLICY: a PIE is an EXECUTABLE -- `allowsUndefinedImports()` FALSE. NO tlsAccess/tdata/tbss (thread_local fails loud, D-LK-DYN-TLS-MODEL). Witnessed under qemu-aarch64 / the ubuntu-24.04-arm CI leg.
$stackReserveUnsupportedReasonComment: D-SQLITE-PE64-FULL-TIER-STACK-DEPTH: ELF has NO image field for a stack SIZE on ANY flavor -- PT_GNU_STACK encodes stack EXECUTABILITY, not size. The kernel sizes the initial thread's stack from the process limit (`ulimit -s` / setrlimit RLIMIT_STACK) and further threads from pthread_attr_setstacksize, so nothing the linker writes can change it. A `stackReserve` / `--stack-reserve` request is therefore REFUSED with that remedy rather than silently dropped -- which is also why the sqlite full tier passes on Linux (8 MiB by default) and overflowed on Windows at 1 MiB.
$dataModelComment: Same LP64 identity as the aarch64 exec/dyn/rel siblings (64-bit Linux).
$headerNameMatchingComment: D-PP-HEADER-CASE-INSENSITIVE-PE: Linux/POSIX header names are matched BYTE-EXACT -- `#include <Stdio.h>` does NOT name `stdio.h`, and a conforming toolchain must reject it. REQUIRED closed-enum field: the loader rejects a missing or unknown value. DSS performs the comparison ITSELF (core/types/include_path_resolve.cpp) rather than calling fs::exists and inheriting the BUILD HOST's convention -- without that, an elf target built on Windows/macOS silently ACCEPTED `<Stdio.h>` and emitted a real object (MEASURED 2026-08-04).
$cSymbolDecorationComment: D-FFI-CMANGLING-RULE-NOT-CONFIG-DRIVEN: System V / ELF applies NO decoration to a C identifier -- the linker-visible name IS the identifier. MEASURED 2026-08-06 (`nm -D /lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libc.so.6`, WSL Ubuntu): glibc exports `exit@@GLIBC_2.2.5`, `printf@@GLIBC_2.2.5` and `fstat64@@GLIBC_2.33` under exactly their C spellings. THE SAME COMMAND IS ALSO WHY `none` IS A POSITIVE ANSWER AND NOT AN ABSENCE: `_exit@@GLIBC_2.2.5` is exported TOO and is a DIFFERENT FUNCTION -- POSIX `_exit(2)`, which does NOT flush stdio -- so a format that wrongly claimed `leading-underscore` would not merely produce an ugly name, it would silently bind every `exit` to the non-flushing wrapper and lose buffered output. This key is the single owner of a fact that previously had TWO: the closed C++ table `kCManglingRules` (src/ffi/mangling/c_mangle.cpp, keyed on ObjectFormatKind) and, redundantly, a literal encoding in the descriptors themselves -- the macho64-*-exec files spell `processExit.importMangledName` as `_exit` while their elf/pe siblings spell it `exit`. Two owners in two languages, with nothing forcing them to agree. RED-ON-DISABLE, stated precisely for the tier that exists today (MEASURED 2026-08-06 by actually removing the key from a shipped file and running the suite): DELETE this key and the format is REFUSED AT LOAD -- TWO errors at /cSymbolDecoration, one C_MissingField from the loader and one from ObjectFormatData::validate(), which loadFromText runs before returning -- so every test and example that loads this format goes red, naming the file. CHANGING the value is now an equally REAL lever, and this sentence was corrected the moment it became true: before step C4 the engine still read a C++ table and the value here changed no emitted binary. C4 landed (same cycle, TF-C122), and the effect is MEASURED 2026-08-06 -- flipping macho64-arm64-darwin-exec from `leading-underscore` to `none` and RECOMPILING NOTHING made the engine emit `printf` where it had emitted `_printf`, reddening tests/ffi/test_c_mangle.cpp's SchemeIsReadFromTheShippedSchemaNotACppTable. That is the whole point of the anchor: the answer lives in this file, so editing this file changes what the compiler emits. Two further pins guard the value: tests/link/test_c_symbol_decoration.cpp asserts the per-kind answer across all 24 shipped files and cross-checks it against this family's own processExit.importMangledName.
$predefinedMacrosComment: TF-C97 (D-PP-FORMAT-DATA-MODEL-PREDEFINES): the C-visible face of this file's `dataModel` above, DERIVED FROM THAT VALUE AND NEVER FROM THIS FILE'S NAME -- the loader synthesizes no macro name and the engine performs no format-identity branch; it merges whatever rows are declared here with the language's `preprocess.predefinedMacros` and the target's `predefinedMacros`, applying `availableObjectFormats` exactly once. DECLARED ON THE FORMAT because the data model is per-(OS x format), not per-CPU: the same x86_64 target is LP64 here and LLP64 under pe64-x86_64-windows-*, so a target-side row would be wrong on one of its own formats -- which is exactly what both .target.json files say when they record `__LP64__`/`_LP64` as DELIBERATELY NOT SHIPPED and defer to the format. BOTH spellings, each value 1: MEASURED 2026-07-30 with `/usr/bin/clang -dM -E -x c /dev/null -target <triple>` (Apple clang 21.0.0), __LP64__ and _LP64 are BOTH defined as 1 on arm64-apple-darwin, x86_64-apple-darwin, aarch64-linux-gnu and x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu, and NEITHER is defined on x86_64-pc-windows-msvc. COLLISION POLICY: a name declared by this file AND the language or target config is FATAL (C_ConflictingPredefinedMacro) -- no side silently wins. WHAT IT UNBLOCKS, MEASURED: the macOS SDK gates 234 occurrences across 91 headers on __LP64__, so without these rows DSS compiled the SDK's ILP32 arms while its own widths were LP64 (sizeof(long)==8), and $SDK/usr/include/mach/port.h:113-114 then asserted the user32 struct size 12 instead of user64's 16 -- sqlite mem1.c's three error[S0029]. RED-ON-DISABLE: delete this key and examples/c-subset/predefined_lp64_macho stops exiting 42.
$bitFieldStrategyComment: D-CSUBSET-BITFIELD-ABI-EXACT: Linux arm64 (AAPCS64) uses the generic LSB-first bit-field allocation -- same gnu_packed as the aarch64 ELF siblings.
$externCallDispatchComment: Same call-site shape as the arm64 exec image and the .so: the walker synthesizes a 16-byte ARM64 PLT stub per extern FUNCTION (ADRP+LDR+BR through the GOT slot, GLOB_DAT eager-bound) and the call site is a plain direct `BL` to the stub -- pc-relative, slide-safe under the ET_DYN load slide. D-FFI-EXTERN-CALL-DISPATCH.
$dataImportBindingComment: extern library DATA objects bind GOT-INDIRECT -- the walker reserves a GOT slot per imported object and emits R_AARCH64_GLOB_DAT against it; ld.so writes the object's address into the slot and the GotIndirect lowering reads it. Copy relocations are the FIXED-BASE ET_EXEC mechanism; validate() rejects copy-relocation on any ET_DYN schema, PIE included.
$supportedDataSectionsComment: rodata (read-only, R+X PT_LOAD #1 -- reloc-FREE items only; a reloc-bearing rodata item would need a load-time write into a read-only page, D-LK-DYN-RODATA-ITEM-RELOC fails loud), data (mutable initialized globals, R+W PT_LOAD #2), bss (zero-init NOBITS tail), relro (reloc-bearing CONST data, c145 -- merged into `.data` so its R_AARCH64_RELATIVE slots land in writable pages). NO tdata/tbss: thread_local fails loud at the MIR->LIR gate / linker section gate (D-LK-DYN-TLS-MODEL).
$artifactProfilesComment: This format SERVES the runnable-console-binary profile (plan 06 AP3) -- a PIE is an executable, so cli, exactly like the ET_EXEC sibling. The lib profile is the .so (elf64-aarch64-linux-dyn).
$entryPointComment: Empty entryPoint defaults the walker to module.functions[0] -- after the linker prepends the synthetic `_start` trampoline (keyed on processExit presence) that IS the trampoline, so e_entry = the trampoline's base-relative VA. The USER entry resolves via module.userEntrySymbol.
$runtimeLibrariesComment: UCRT-P4 (D-FFI-PE-CRT-UCRT-MIGRATION): the ROLE -> IMAGE table, and the SINGLE OWNER of 'which image plays which runtime role' for this format. The spine blocks below name a ROLE and the loader resolves it here; each block's resolved path is a DERIVED copy and ObjectFormatData::validate() re-checks the pair, so the two cannot drift. The table is not a pe concern that ELF merely inherits -- ELF is where the SPLIT IS ALREADY REAL, and that is the measured argument for a table over a single per-format CRT string: MEASURED 2026-08-10 (`nm -D`), the unwinder personality lives in libgcc_s.so.1 and libc.so.6 exports NO `_Unwind_*` symbol at all. Do NOT be fooled by `personality@@GLIBC_2.2.5` in libc -- that is the personality(2) SYSCALL wrapper, unrelated to unwinding. So on this format one image demonstrably cannot serve both cLibrary and unwindPersonality, whereas on pe64 they happen to coincide (ucrtbase exports `__C_specific_handler` at ord 30) -- a table PERMITS that sameness without ASSERTING it. This file declares only cLibrary today because it names only cLibrary: an unwindPersonality row would be INERT until ELF unwind lands and a `sehPersonality`-equivalent block names it, and validate() REFUSES an unnamed row rather than letting a stale image sit here unread. RED-ON-DISABLE: delete this row and processExit refuses the format AT LOAD, naming this file.
$entryVerbsComment: UCRT-P4 (D-RUNTIME-MAIN-ENVP-ENTRY-SHAPE): the program-entry materialization VERBS THIS FORMAT CAN REALIZE -- what it is able to hand a program entry before calling it. * THE ACCEPTED ENTRY SET IS AN INTERSECTION, AND THIS FILE OWNS ONLY HALF OF IT. This key used to be `entryShapes` -- full { returns, params, materialization } rows -- which made the accepted SIGNATURES a format fact. They are not one: `int wmain(int, wchar_t**)` is a C spelling, and a linker format has no opinion on how a source language spells an entry, only on what it can hand one. So the signatures moved to their single owner, the language file's `entryFunctions` mapping (src/dss-config/sources/c-subset.lang.json), which declares each name->signature->verb; this key declares the VERBS THIS FORMAT CAN REALIZE. A defined function is a program-entry candidate iff its name matches a declared language row, its signature matches that row, and that row's verb appears HERE. C23 3.4.1 requires an implementation to DOCUMENT its implementation-defined choices, so the documentation artifact is the PAIR of comments -- this one and $entryFunctionsComment -- each naming the other. Reading either alone tells you less than the truth. * WHY `argc-wargv` IS ABSENT, AND WHAT THAT NOW ACHIEVES: nothing on this platform produces a wide argument vector, so this format cannot realize the verb. That absence is the entire mechanism by which `wmain` is not a program entry here -- the language still declares `wmain -> argc-wargv`, the verb is not in this set, so the row does not survive the intersection and `wmain` is an ordinary function. MEASURED 2026-08-10 on HEAD 3e86a187 (build-dbg), BEFORE this: `int wmain(int, unsigned short**)` with no `main`, built for this format, was SELECTED AS THE LINUX ENTRY by a name-only scan and then refused by a message that asserted `wmain` WAS the Linux entry and prescribed adding a row to this very file to make it one. gcc's answer to that source is `undefined reference to 'main'`. A `main` + `wmain` program now BUILDS here and takes `main`, because exactly one candidate survives. * WHY THERE IS NO envp VERB YET, and why that is a cycle rather than a data addition: on ELF envp CANNOT be a third static offset -- processArgs above declares STATIC argcStackOffset/argvStackOffset, whereas envp sits at argv_base + (argc+1)*8, i.e. RUNTIME-COMPUTED. A new verb needs its own emitter and its own RUN witness (D-RUNTIME-MAIN-ENVP-ENTRY-SHAPE). * `none` is the verb `int main(void)` needs -- C23's () == (void) equivalence makes `int main()` resolve to it -- and declaring it is an ANSWER, not an omission: a no-argument entry needs no setup at all. * RED-ON-DISABLE: drop "argc-argv" from this list and every example whose entry is `main(int, char**)` becomes unresolvable on this format -- the language's argc-argv row no longer survives the intersection, so the program has no entry candidate at all and the build is REFUSED naming this key. Empty the list entirely and the format is refused AT LOAD (exec-flavored <-> non-empty entryVerbs is pinned in both directions), because the engine reads this emptiness as "this format starts no program".
$processExitComment: ENTRY CLUSTER member (the PIE discriminator). Identical to the aarch64 ET_EXEC sibling: terminate via libc `exit(3)` by-name-import (STDIO-FLUSH-AT-EXIT). The trampoline emits a DIRECT `BL` to the PLT stub for `exit` (per externCallDispatch=direct-plt) -- pc-relative, slide-safe. libc.so.6 becomes a DT_NEEDED; ld-linux-aarch64 resolves the GOT slot eagerly (DF_1_NOW).
$entryCallingConventionComment: ENTRY CLUSTER member. AAPCS64 -- the user fn's return value (x0) is moved into argGprs[0] = x0 before the exit call. Read via `target.callingConventionByName("aapcs64")` at trampoline-build time.
$processArgsComment: ENTRY CLUSTER member. c88 (D-RUNTIME-MAIN-ARGC-ARGV): AAPCS64 Linux mirrors the SysV stack-vector layout -- argc at [sp+0], the NULL-terminated argv vector IN PLACE at [sp+8]; ld.so transfers control to a PIE's e_entry with this exact layout. The trampoline emits `LDUR x0,[sp,#0]` + `ADD x1, sp, #8` before any SP adjustment and before `BL main`.

elf.$comment: Elf64_Ehdr identity for an arm64 PIE. type = ET_DYN (3) -- a PIE IS a shared object to the kernel/loader; what makes it an EXECUTABLE is the entry cluster + the resulting non-zero e_entry + PT_INTERP. machine = 183 (EM_AARCH64). pageAlign = 4096. interpreter = the PT_INTERP path (/lib/ld-linux-aarch64.so.1 -- the kernel maps ld.so, which relocates the image at a randomized base and jumps to base + e_entry). NO soname (validate-rejected with the entry cluster). bindNow = true: DT_FLAGS_1 = DF_1_NOW | DF_1_PIE.

sections.$comment: Executable code. virtualAddress = 4096 = elf.pageAlign, PINNED by validate() for every ET_DYN schema (base-0 by construction; page zero holds Ehdr + PHT + .interp + dynamic metadata). sh_flags = SHF_ALLOC|SHF_EXECINSTR (6).
sections.name: .text

sections.$comment: Read-only initialized data. Folded into R+X PT_LOAD #1 after .text. virtualAddress = 0 -- computed. A reloc-bearing const global goes to relro instead (c145).
sections.name: .rodata

sections.$comment: Writable initialized data. R+W PT_LOAD #2. virtualAddress = 0 -- computed.
sections.name: .data

sections.$comment: Zero-initialized data. SHT_NOBITS (8); memsz-only tail of PT_LOAD #2. virtualAddress = 0 -- computed.
sections.name: .bss

relocations.$comment: 26-bit PC-relative branch-with-link (BL) -- the extern-call reloc on a PLT stub. Legal in ET_DYN `.text` (pc-relative). kind = 1 = arm64.target.json's `call26`.
relocations.name: R_AARCH64_CALL26

relocations.$comment: ADRP page-base pc-relative (high 21 bits). Legal in `.text` (pc-relative). kind = 2 = `adr_prel_pg_hi21`.
relocations.name: R_AARCH64_ADR_PREL_PG_HI21

relocations.$comment: ADD low-12 absolute (no check) -- the pair with ADRP. kind = 3 = `add_abs_lo12_nc`.
relocations.name: R_AARCH64_ADD_ABS_LO12_NC

relocations.$comment: abs64 -- DATA items only: the walker patches the slot with the base-relative value AND emits an R_AARCH64_RELATIVE (1027) row (the load slide completes the address); an extern-targeted slot emits a symbol-based R_AARCH64_ABS64 row with the slot zeroed. kind = 4 = `abs64`.
relocations.name: R_AARCH64_ABS64
